schemes.name: DEI+ (Demonstratie Energie- en Klimaatinnovatie)
schemes.summary: Demonstration projects that cut CO2 or scale renewable energy.
schemes.ignite_tags: sector: Energy, Environment & Sustainability | size: All company sizes | scope: National | topic: Climate & Energy | type: Grant
schemes.aliases: DEI+ themes: Energie- en klimaatinnovaties; Vergassing van reststromen; Verduurzaming gebouwde omgeving; Circulaire economie en grootschalige biobased; Biobased Circular
schemes.legal_basis: DEI+ rules in the national EZ, LVVN and KGG subsidies regulation; Staatscourant 18 Dec 2025 (nr. 43110 and 42972); Handleiding DEI+ 2026
schemes.status: Mixed by theme. Closed on 30 Jul 2026: energy and climate innovations, gasification of residual streams, hydrogen and green chemistry, Biobased Circular (small). Closed 27 Aug 2026: built environment. OPEN to 17 Dec 2026: circular economy and Biobased Circular large projects (combined EUR 60M).
schemes.applicants: Individual companies acting at their own cost and risk, or participants in a partnership with at least one company; provinces and municipalities may join but cannot receive subsidy; water boards can in some cases. Applies in NL including Bonaire, St Eustatius and Saba.
schemes.funding_rate: Maximum rates (Handleiding 2026): pilots 25% for companies (80% for research bodies' non-economic activity); test infrastructure 25%; demonstrations: environmental or other CO2 measures 40% of extra investment cost (30% for CCS/CCU; halved if no reference scenario); energy efficiency 30% of extra cost; energy efficiency in buildings 25% of total cost; renewable energy and renewable hydrogen 45% (30% for storage or specific hydrogen infrastructure); circular economy 40% of extra cost; infrastructure 30% (art. 46) or 50% (art. 56); gasification 40-45% by category. Uplift for all project types: +10 points medium and +20 points small firms.
schemes.caps: Demonstration up to EUR 30M; pilot and test infrastructure up to EUR 25M; built environment EUR 1M; Biobased Circular pilot EUR 1M and demonstration EUR 10M (large-project sub-theme above those amounts up to EUR 25M and 30M); gasification EUR 30M; built-environment de minimis support EUR 300,000 per company over 36 months
schemes.budget: Regular themes EUR 134M; built environment EUR 6M; circular economy and Biobased Circular large EUR 60M; Biobased Circular EUR 22M; hydrogen and green chemistry EUR 38M; gasification EUR 150M
schemes.stacking: Other national subsidies reduce DEI+ support; SDE++, Horizon, provincial and municipal subsidies are not deducted in advance
schemes.eligible_costs: Pilots: wages plus 50% overhead, or fixed EUR 80 per hour (raised from EUR 60 in 2026), or full-cost method, plus depreciation of equipment, materials and third-party costs. Demonstrations: extra investment costs against a reference investment, or total investment costs depending on the GBER article.
schemes.channel: RVO portal; eHerkenning level 3
schemes.window: Themes have separate windows; circular economy and large biobased: 16 Jun to 17 Dec 2026
schemes.before_start: Yes: no start, order or commitment before the application is filed; start within 6 months of the grant; project max 4 years; CO2 reduction in NL within 10 years of the start
schemes.assessment: First come, first served by date of complete application; 8 weeks, extendable by 8; positive decisions sent by mid-December because the budget is for 2026 only
schemes.fit_signals: Industrial or energy pilot of an innovation with CO2 or energy savings, in food and agri, industry or energy
schemes.related: VEKI (proven technology); STUDI (studies); SDE++; EU Innovation Fund
schemes.confidence: High: rates, caps, budgets, windows and conditions from RVO's DEI+ pages and the 2026 Handleiding

sources.field: circular economy theme, open to 17 Dec

schemes.conflicts: RESOLVED: Ignite lists one DEI+ row; RVO runs separate themes with their own budgets and windows, now recorded here. Windows verified against the Handleiding table.
schemes.open_questions: Subsidy percentages for the hydrogen theme's non-renewable cases and gasification categories are summarised, not tabulated per category

schemes.name: DHI (Demonstratieprojecten, Haalbaarheidsstudies, Investeringsvoorbereidingsprojecten)
schemes.summary: Demonstration, feasibility and investment-preparation projects in foreign markets.
schemes.ignite_tags: sector: All sectors | size: ≤250 employees | scope: National | topic: International | type: Grant
schemes.legal_basis: DHI regulation, Staatscourant 2026, nr. 7891
schemes.status: OPEN 2 Mar to 31 Dec 2026, or until the budget is used; assessed in order of arrival (RVO pages checked 30 Oct 2026)
schemes.applicants: SMEs with legal personality (not sole traders, VOF, CV or maatschap) in NL or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom, registered at KVK; collaborations may include a large company. Needs at least 3 employees in NL, EUR 100,000 turnover over the last 3 years, no other DHI project running, and de minimis headroom (EUR 300,000 over 3 years).
schemes.size_rule: SME with legal personality; at least 3 employees in NL (structural hiring counts); EUR 100,000 turnover over 3 years
schemes.funding_rate: 50% of project costs, or 70% for green projects (climate or circular economy; RVO screening framework), for demonstration, feasibility and investment-preparation projects. Minimum subsidy EUR 25,000 (costs of at least EUR 50,000).
schemes.caps: Demonstration up to EUR 200,000 (max 3 years); feasibility up to EUR 100,000 (max 2 years); investment preparation up to EUR 100,000, and in 2026 time costs in NL and abroad together max EUR 75,000; market validation (new in 2026) EUR 25,000 for start-ups up to ten years old when costs are at least EUR 50,000, max 40 in 2026 (20 in developing countries, 20 elsewhere)
schemes.budget: EUR 8.5M for 2026 (RVO news, 2 Mar 2026)
schemes.instrument_detail: Four parts: demonstration, feasibility study, investment preparation, market validation. Technology must be TRL 8 or 9 for demonstration and feasibility. Export of at least 10 times the subsidy (5 times in developing countries) within 3 years of a demonstration; investment of at least 5 times the subsidy within 3 years of an investment-preparation project.
schemes.stacking: De minimis ceiling EUR 300,000 over three years
schemes.eligible_costs: Demonstration: hardware by depreciation, transport and related costs; time spent in NL may not exceed time spent abroad. Feasibility: study costs and a report for the foreign customer; no market research. Investment preparation: study, small trial production, outside expertise up to 50% of costs.
schemes.excluded_costs: Developing new technology or adapting the product for the foreign market; sales activities such as quotations and promotional material; selling the demonstration hardware to the host
schemes.channel: RVO e-Loket with eHerkenning level 2+ (RVO login for the Caribbean); quick scan available by email before applying
schemes.window: 2 Mar 2026 to 31 Dec 2026, or until the budget is used (first come, first served)
schemes.before_start: RVO says that once an application is approved, work can start; the exact start-date rule sits in the regulation text (Staatscourant 2026, 7891) and was not read
schemes.assessment: Order of arrival; 90% advance on approval; yearly progress report for projects over 1 year; payout request within 13 weeks of completion; decision on it within 13 weeks; management statement needed for subsidies of EUR 125,000 or more
schemes.per_period_limit: Only one running DHI project at a time
schemes.fit_signals: Dutch SME proving technology to foreign buyers or preparing a foreign investment
schemes.confidence: High: rates, caps, eligibility, window, budget and post-award rules from RVO's four DHI pages and the process page

sources.field: after you apply (advance, reporting, final decision)

schemes.conflicts: RESOLVED: the earlier consultancy rate gap is closed; RVO states 50% or 70%. Earlier note that time costs in investment preparation are capped at EUR 75,000 is confirmed.
schemes.open_questions: Read Staatscourant 7891 for the exact start-date rule

schemes.name: EIC Accelerator
schemes.summary: EU grant-plus-equity funding for innovative SMEs with scaling potential.
schemes.ignite_tags: sector: Digital & IT | size: All company sizes | scope: EU | topic: Digitalisation | type: Grant
schemes.authority: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA); EIC Fund for equity
schemes.legal_basis: EIC Work Programme 2026 (Horizon Europe Pillar III)
schemes.status: Rolling. The 2027 work programme was adopted on 5 Nov 2026 (EIC total EUR 1.8bn). Short proposals can be filed at any time; full proposals are batched on 20 Jan, 17 Mar, 1 Sep and 4 Nov 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. Latest result: 35 companies selected on 16 Nov 2026 (EUR 84M in grants, 32 of them assessed for equity of up to EUR 10M).
schemes.applicants: SMEs in a Member State or Associated Country; small mid-caps (up to 499 employees) only for investment-only support, or blended finance in exceptional rapid-scale-up cases; natural persons or entities intending to set up an SME there, or to invest in one, or non-associated-country founders intending to set up or relocate an SME into the EU or an Associated Country
schemes.size_rule: SMEs and small mid-caps (a small mid-cap has up to 499 employees)
schemes.stage: Technology validated in a relevant environment (TRL 5 complete); gap to TRL 8
schemes.funding_rate: Grant covers 70% of eligible costs (30% co-financing); lump sum
schemes.caps: Grant up to EUR 2.5M for innovation activities (TRL 6 to 8); investment component EUR 1M to EUR 10M (TRL 6 to 9) as equity or convertible loan; grant-only is possible under conditions and only once during Horizon Europe 2021 to 2027. Higher amounts through STEP Scale Up.
schemes.budget: 2027: Accelerator Open EUR 428M and Accelerator Challenges EUR 150M. (2026: EUR 634M overall.)
schemes.instrument_detail: Lump-sum grant plus optional equity
schemes.channel: EU Funding & Tenders portal: short proposal (12-page form, 10 slides, 3-minute video), full proposal, jury interview, agreement
schemes.window: Full-proposal batching dates for 2027: 20 Jan, 17 Mar, 1 Sep, 4 Nov 2027 (5pm Brussels). The 2026 batching dates (7 Jan, 4 Mar, 6 May, 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026) have all passed.
schemes.before_start: Not stated on the EIC web page; grant agreement is prepared after the award and the investment goes through due diligence by the EIC Fund
schemes.assessment: Four steps: short proposal (12-page form, 10-slide deck, 3-minute video; feedback in about 4 to 6 weeks, optional coach); full proposal (20-page form, deck, video, annexes on finance and cap table, IP and FTO, implementation plan and lump-sum table for the grant part); expert plus panel evaluation; jury interview held twice a year. A score of 13 out of 15 at remote evaluation without an invitation earns a Seal of Excellence.
schemes.per_period_limit: After three unsuccessful submissions an applicant is barred; one live application at a time (aggregator reading of rules)
schemes.fit_signals: Deep-tech or hardware/software scale-up with validated technology and a financing gap
schemes.rejection_risks: Not enough evidence of market creation or financing gap; TRL too low
schemes.related: STEP Scale Up; Eurostars; Horizon Europe
schemes.confidence: High on amounts and dates (multiple sources); success rate and barring rule are secondary

sources.field: EIC Accelerator page: 2027 batching dates, budgets, eligibility, process

schemes.summary: Reduced effective corporate tax rate on profits from innovation.
schemes.ignite_tags: sector: All sectors | size: All company sizes | scope: National | topic: Innovation | type: Tax incentive
schemes.authority: Belastingdienst (executes); RVO S&O statement is the access ticket
schemes.legal_basis: Corporate income tax act 1969, art. 12b
schemes.status: Open every year through the corporate income tax return (Belastingdienst guidance on business.gov.nl)
schemes.applicants: Companies liable to Dutch corporate income tax with legal personality (such as a BV or NV) that developed the intangible asset themselves, at their own cost and risk, under an R&D declaration (S&O verklaring) from RVO obtained through WBSO. schemes.size_rule: Smaller versus larger taxpayer, set by turnover and income from intellectual property; thresholds are on the Belastingdienst's Dutch page and were not read
schemes.funding_rate: Qualifying innovation profit is taxed at an effective 9% instead of 19% (up to EUR 200,000) or 25.8% (above EUR 200,000)
schemes.caps: Box threshold: benefits count only after development costs are recouped. Flat-rate option: 25% of profit, max EUR 25,000 base per year (RVO brochure, 2024 edition).
schemes.instrument_detail: Larger taxpayers need, besides the R&D declaration, a legal access ticket (a patent or pending patent, plant breeders' right, software, a licence to market new medicines, a registered utility model, or a supplementary protection certificate) and, if the ticket is a patent, at least 30% of the profit must be due to the patent. There is only one innovation box for all innovations.
schemes.eligible_costs: Box threshold: R&D costs previously deducted from taxable profit must first be offset before profit enters the box; outsourcing to related companies reduces the qualifying share (nexus approach)
schemes.excluded_costs: Brands and logos; losses (they go in the regular box and can be carried back one year and forward)
schemes.channel: Tax return; requires an S&O statement from WBSO
schemes.before_start: WBSO must be applied for before the R&D starts, because the R&D declaration is the entry ticket
schemes.assessment: Self-assessed in the annual corporate income tax return; the Belastingdienst checks the administration: the innovative assets, total profit and how it was calculated
schemes.post_award: Keep development-cost records for the box threshold
schemes.fit_signals: Profitable Dutch company with WBSO statements and self-developed IP or software
schemes.rejection_risks: No S&O statement; larger taxpayer without patent or equivalent right
schemes.confidence: High on the 9% rate, conditions and extra conditions for larger taxpayers (Belastingdienst guidance published on business.gov.nl); small-versus-large thresholds not read
schemes.conflicts: None found: PwC and BDO summaries agree on 9% against 25.8% for 2026.
